executive_summary: This lecture examines MLOps engineering, reproducibility, and production machine learning systems. Transitioning a machine learning prototype from an experimental notebook into a reliable enterprise system requires rigorous software engineering discipline. Model checkpoints and datasets should be tracked with explicit version tags, training timestamps, and SHA-256 cryptographic checksums to guarantee artifact provenance. Monolithic scripts that mix user interface code, data ingestion, model inference, and evaluation logic are brittle and difficult to maintain.

section_summaries.section_summary: This lecture examines MLOps engineering, reproducibility, and production machine learning systems. Transitioning a machine learning prototype from an experimental notebook into a reliable enterprise system requires rigorous software engineering discipline.
Model checkpoints and datasets should be tracked with explicit version tags, training timestamps, and SHA-256 cryptographic checksums to guarantee artifact provenance.

Monolithic scripts that mix user interface code, data ingestion, model inference, and evaluation logic are brittle and difficult to maintain. Automated tests suites built with pytest verify both unit functionality and boundary conditions before any code change is merged.

Regression tests ensure that updates to heuristic post-processors or configuration thresholds do not silently degrade established precision or formatting standards. The module focuses on inference optimization, fault tolerance, and operational telemetry.
When deploying speech recognition and transformer summarization models, engineers track operational metrics alongside statistical quality metrics.

This lecture addresses post-deployment monitoring, data drift detection, and human in the loop feedback loops. Unlike static software, machine learning models degrade over time as real-world input distributions shift away from historical training data.
This lecture examines containerization, dependency pinning, and continuous integration workflows.
A common source of production failures is environment skew between a data scientist local workstation and the cloud inference server.
This lecture analyzes shadow deployments, canary releases, and A/B testing strategies for validating new model versions safely in production.
